raw_response:
I farm only 2.2 mu, so I count every bag and every trip to the field. I have done wheat-maize for many years, and with well water I will not let the crop go thirsty at the key times. I do not like making big changes. I start from what I used before, then I adjust a little if I think the stand was weak or the ears were not full. On small land like mine, if I save a little fertilizer and lose yield, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on one more bag. So I will keep the land in wheat-maize, use better seed, feed wheat a bit heavier because it stays longer in the field, and give maize enough nitrogen so it can push ears. For wheat, I will put most phosphorus at sowing, split nitrogen between base and spring topdressing, water around sowing if dry, once at greening or jointing, and once at filling if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, put base fertilizer under the row, then chase nitrogen before big flare, and water after sowing if dry, once around jointing, and once around silking if the weather is hot. I usually rotary till because my area is small and it is faster and cheaper than deep ploughing every season. For pests and disease, I will not spray too many times, but I will not skip the important ones either: wheat for aphid or rust if I see it, maize for armyworm or corn borer if it comes. I will aim for a steady harvest, not gambling on saving a few yuan.
